messages:
sam: FYI planning to add TTL on runtime overrides so temporary changes auto-expire.

nina: Nice. Is this going to be per-route? per-actor? per-flag?

sam: Per-route and per-scope (route/service/global). API sketch:
```
POST /runtime/overrides
{
  "route": "inference.v1.generate",
  "scope": "route",
  "overrides": {"max_tokens": 1024},
  "ttl_seconds": 7200,
  "created_by": "sam"
}
```

priya: What's the failure mode? We should avoid auto-reverting during investigations.

mike: We should gate auto-expiry with telemetry: don't auto-expire if there's an active rollback block (e.g., linked incident) OR if the change caused a regression (latency/quality) within the TTL.

sam: Agreed. Proposal: expiry is scheduled but runtime evaluates a pre-check hook before finalizing revert. Hook queries telemetry service and incidents API. If a regression signal exists, we keep the override and flag for manual review.

rachel: That sounds complex. How do we avoid a race where telemetry lags and we revert incorrectly?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled expiry for override id 0x7f2 in 2h

sam: To reduce risk, default behavior: send 24h warning to the owner + create a console "expiry pending" state (yellow) 6h before TTL. Console can Extend/Cancel.

nina: Console changes: need column for "expires at", hover shows reason, extend button with audit modal. Also bulk extend for multiple overrides.

priya: Audit/logs: every auto-revert must create an immutable audit entry with before/after config, who triggered, telemetry snapshot link.

mike: Migration: what do we do with current permanent overrides? We should backfill them with ttl=null and mark created_at. For safety-run, we can add 'soft-ttl' for old ones so ops can clean up.

sam: I'll open a migration PR that tags existing overrides with created_by and created_at. Then operator CLI to list filters "stale-overrides --older-than=30d".

rachel: API rate/permission notes: only allow ttl for users with override:write. Also rate-limit override creation per-route to avoid thrash.

priya: Also need to document interactions with quota routing: if a short-lived override routes to a more expensive model, we need to surface estimated cost delta before apply.

mike: Telemetry check list: latency p95, error-rate delta, generation-quality metric (evaluations) if available. If any exceed thresholds the auto-revert is blocked and an alert to #incidents created.

sam: UX can show a small "cost delta" and "safety score" before apply. Default TTL 4h for devs, 72h for oncall-created.

nina: Can we canary the feature? Roll to 10% of org (eng-platform) for 48h. Add feature flag runtime.override.ttl.

sam: Yep. I'll push a canary flag + console toggle. deploy-bot: rolling canary to eng-platform 10% now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/runtime-ttl v1 -> pods: 3 -> 3. link: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4321

priya: Next steps: sam make RFC + PR, nina do console mockups, mike kick off telemetry gating prototype.

sam: On it. I'll ping when PRs are ready. :thumbsup:
